name: Statue of Dupleix Puducherry
description: The French capital of India, Puducherry, erstwhile Pondicherry, showcases a perfect blend of Indian and French culture. From the evergreen beaches to the colourful buildings and quaint cafes, the streets of Puducherry come alive with enthusiasm every day. However, what justifies the blend is the Statue of Dupleix standing on Goubert Avenue. The statue is of the last French governor in Puducherry, Joseph Francois Dupleix.

name: Varadharaja Perumal Temple Puducherry
description: One of the oldest temples in Pondicherry is Varadharaja Perumal Temple. Dedicated to the Hindu community, the Varadharaja Perumal Temple offers holy and mystical vibes to the devotees of Lord Vishnu and boasts a kind of atmosphere that lets you forget everything about your day-to-day life for some time. Venkatachalapathy is the principal deity here and behind his idol, one can also find the idol of Lord Narsimha, who is an incarnation of Lord Vishnu itself.

name: Veerampattinam Beach Puducherry
description: Sitting by the waters of the Bay of Bengal, Puducherry is the eastern French Riviera. Although every bit of the UT has details of French settlers, it is unmistakably Indian. Veerampattinam is one of the biggest coastal villages between Puducherry and Cuddalore. The river surrounds the village on both sides that protects it from cyclones.
